" At the outset, may we invite our attention the following provisions of Republic Act No. 7160 or thé Local Governme t Code of 1991, viz: "SEC. 22 (c) Unless o erwise provided in this Code, no contract may be entered into by the local chie executive in behalfofthe local government unit without prior authorization by e sanggunian€concerned. A legible copy of such contract shall be posted ata cons .icuousplacein theprovincialcapitolor the city, m unicipality or barangay hall. " SEC. 444 (b) (l) (vi). Upon authorization by the sangguniang bayan, represent the municipality in a its business transactions and sign on its behalf all bonds, contracts, and obligatio s, and such other documents made pursuant to law or ordinance. xvx" In reply to your first query based on the aforequoted provisions of the Local Government Code of 1991, the Muni ipal Mayor may enter into contracts, for and in behalf of the municipality (1) if made upon uthority of the sanggunian, or (2) pursuant to law or ordinance. In the latter case, if a law or n ordinance already authorizes the Municipal Mayor to enter into a contract, prior authori ation from the Sanggunian concerned is not anymore required. Such law or ordinance serv s as an authority for the Mayor to enter such contract. This is precisely the exception bein referred by the phrase "(U)nless Otherwise provided

in this Code" in the opening statem t of Section 22 (c) of the Local Government Code of 1991. Ergo, the Mayor may represe t the municipality in all its contracts even Without a prior authorization from the Sang iang Bayan, for as long as there is either a LAW or ORDINANCE that authorizes him/h r to do so. If there is no law or ordinan e authorizingßhe Mayor to enter such contract, the same falls within the first case d therefore requires prior authorization from the Sangguniang Bayan. As to your second query, pl se note that when a local chief executive enters or negotiates a contract in behalf of the ocal government unit, he is acting as a mere agent of the local government unit. Contract entered into by the local chief executive without the requisite prior authority given by th local sanggunian concerned shall make the contract unauthorized or unenforceable. Art cle 1317, 2nd paragraph, and Article 1403 [1] of the New Civil Code, specifically provide that "a contract entered into in the name ofanother by one who has no authority or lega representation, or who has acted beyond his powers, shall be unenforceable, xxx". If such defect is .theréafterfo d by the Commission on Audit (COA), under the New Civil Code, unauthorized or enforceable contracts are susceptible to ratification. Contracts entered into by the Mun • ipal Mayor may be cured from its defect after the Sangguniang Bayan shall have passe a resolution ratifying the same. We hope to have guided you ccordingly.
